name: @reactunity/renderer
//exports: `./tests` is the entry that exists: the source file is tests.ts and packages/scripts/lib/types/tests.d.ts references `@reactunity/renderer/tests`. The map only ever declared `./test`, pointed at ./dist/test.js -- a name tsc never emitted -- so both spellings failed to resolve under an exports-aware resolver. `./test` is kept as an alias for the same file rather than dropped, since it costs nothing and it is the name published so far.
//exports-tailwind: Plain CSS, so `css/` joins `dist/` in `files`. Tailwind reads these through the exports map like any other import; nothing bundles them.
//exports-vite: Node-only, and the one entry a consumer imports outside the Unity bundle -- hence .mjs. This package is not an ESM package, and Vite loads a config file's externalised imports through Node, which would read a .js file here as CommonJS and choke on its imports.
author: Gokhan Kurt <krtgkn@gmail.com> (https://github.com/KurtGokhan)
//peerDependenciesMeta: Only ./vite needs Vite, and only for its types -- the runtime entries never touch it. Tailwind is the app's own dependency; css/tailwind.css imports its theme and utilities, and nothing else here mentions it.
